tagline.text: A clear freshwater swimming pool hidden inside a coral limestone cave in Patar, Bolinao

location.label: Location
location.text: Patar Road, Barangay Patar, Bolinao, Pangasinan

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~1,000 per person (local costs only; Manila round-trip bus not included)

children.text: This coral limestone cave sits inside a privately run park in Patar, Bolinao, and holds a clear, cool freshwater pool at its inner end. It pairs well with Patar Beach and Bolinao Falls for a half-day outing.

Enchanted Cave is a small limestone cave in Barangay Patar on the Bolinao peninsula at the western tip of Pangasinan. It lies along the road from Bolinao town proper (the poblacion) to Patar Beach and is usually the first stop on a Bolinao tour. The cave is inside a privately run park, so you pay an entrance fee at the gate.

The cave formed from hardened coral, so you can see fossilized coral and giant clam traces in the walls and floor. Follow the stairs and concrete path down and you reach a clear freshwater pool in a lit chamber. Although the sea is right next door, the water is fresh rather than salty, and it is cooler than the air outside, which makes it a good place to cool off on a hot day.

Besides the cave, the park has a sand path lined with coconut palms, gardens, small huts for resting, and good photo spots. A white cross stands on the hill, and visitors report that from the top you can see toward the Bolinao lighthouse and the South China Sea (called the West Philippine Sea in the Philippines). Some visitors say an extra fee was charged for the cross, so check on site.

This is not a large attraction. A cave visit and a swim take one to two hours, so most travelers combine it with Patar Beach, Bolinao Falls and the Cape Bolinao Lighthouse for a full day. Because the bus from Manila takes about
6 hours

, I recommend staying at least one night in Bolinao. First-timers often wonder about a few things. First, the cave is narrow and short: it is not an adventure caving route but a walk down the stairs to rest by the water. Second, you can enter without swimming, and sources say the fee differs depending on whether you swim. Third, entrance fees and hours differ by source, so check ahead.

The pool at the inner end of the cave is clear fresh water and cooler than the outside air. Swimming is allowed, and sources say only 16 swimmers are allowed at a time. Depth varies by spot and can change with the tide and season, so follow the staff's instructions.

The cave walls are made of coral and limestone, with traces such as giant clam fossils. It is a place where you can see with your own eyes that this land was once under the sea, which makes it easy to explain to children.

Stairs, railings and lighting are installed, so you can go down without a flashlight. The lit water looks blue and photographs well. The floor is wet and slippery, so step carefully. The cave is cooler than outside, and the water is clear enough that you can see the coral rocks on the bottom.

blocks.title: The white cross on the hill

children.text: A path and stairs lead to the white cross on the park's hill. Visitors report views toward the Bolinao lighthouse and the sea from the top. An extra fee (in the past about
per person) has been charged to climb, so ask at the entrance.

The palm-lined path, gardens and huts make it a pleasant place to rest after a swim. Hut rental is said to vary by size, and some travelers bring a packed lunch. After swimming you need a place to change and rest, so renting a hut is convenient. If your group is large, splitting the rental fee is cheaper.

One visitor reported having the cave almost to themselves for a while just before closing time, after the tour groups had left. Going early in the morning also works, with weaker sun and fewer people.

blocks.title: The first stop on a Bolinao tour

children.text: Because Enchanted Cave lies along the road to Patar Beach, it is often the starting point of a tricycle tour. After the cave, you can continue straight on to Patar Beach and the rock formations.
Take a tricycle from Bolinao town to Patar. It is about
15 minutes
from town.
Arrive at Enchanted Cave park, pay the entrance fee and walk down the stairs into the cave. It is relatively quiet just after opening.
Swim or dip your feet in the freshwater pool and take photos. Listen to the staff's safety instructions first.
Climb to the cross on the hill for the view, or rest in a garden hut.
Head to Patar Beach to walk on the white sand and have lunch.
One to two hours is enough for the cave, so combine it with other sights on the same day.
Leave town and visit Enchanted Cave as your first stop.
Explore Patar Beach and the rock formations along the shore.
Return to town for lunch and see Bolinao Church (St. James the Great Parish).
Head south to Bolinao Falls in Barangay Samang Norte for a swim. It is about
19km
from town, with a dirt road section off the national highway.
Before sunset, go toward the Cape Bolinao Lighthouse or return to your lodging.
A tricycle tour is described as costing around
for four people (as of 2017), so confirm what is included before you negotiate.
Take a direct bus from Manila (Cubao or Pasay) to Bolinao. Five Star, Dagupan Bus and Victory Liner are described as running this route.
The trip takes about
6 hours
, and the fare was from
one way as of 2017. Check current fares and departure times with each bus company.
If you take an overnight bus leaving around midnight, you arrive in Bolinao town around dawn.
Another option is to take an Alaminos-bound bus and then continue about
1 hour
more by bus or van to Bolinao.
After landing at Clark International Airport (CRK), you can transfer at the Angeles terminal to a bus with a "Bolinao" signboard.
Some visitors report taking a Victory Liner bus from the Dau terminal in Mabalacat to Bolinao in four to five hours.
A tricycle from Bolinao town (the poblacion) to Patar takes about
15 minutes
In 2017 the one-way tricycle fare from town to Patar was about
for up to four people. It has often risen since, so confirm the fare before you ride.
If you drive or rent a car, follow Patar Road; there is parking in front of the cave park.
The cave is cooler than outside and can be visited year-round, but if you are also touring the beach and falls, the drier months (November–May) are more convenient.
The midday sun is strong, so going early in the morning is cooler and less crowded. March to May is very hot, but that makes a swim in the cave feel all the better.

On weekends, holidays and in peak season, visitors tend to increase after about 10 a.m., so a weekday morning is best. Some visitors found it quiet just before closing, but that leaves little time, so ask for the last entry time first.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.
Along Patar Beach near the cave there are beach resorts and budget lodging. Bolinao town has places to stay too, so choose to suit your plans. Booking ahead is safer in peak season and on weekends.
For meals, use restaurants in town or near Patar Beach. If you plan to rest in a park hut, bring light snacks and drinks. Opening hours and prices change often, so check locally.

Visiting Enchanted Cave alone as a day trip from Manila is unrealistic. The bus alone takes about 6 hours each way, so it is more practical to spend a night in Bolinao and split the cave, falls, beach and lighthouse over two days. If you stay near Patar Beach, it is easy to reach the cave early in the morning.
Entrance fees vary from ₱150 to ₱300 depending on the review, so check the latest fee and carry plenty of cash in small bills.
Wear non-slip sandals or water shoes. The cave floor is wet.
If you plan to swim, bring swimwear, a towel and a change of clothes. Be careful with phones and other electronics near the water.
Early morning or just before closing is relatively quiet. At midday, when groups arrive, you may have to wait.
Hours are generally described as about
to
, but sources differ slightly. If you arrive late, you may not be admitted.
Do not touch the rock formations or coral in the cave, and follow the rules.
Planning one day with Patar Beach and Bolinao Falls lets you split the tricycle fare.
Call the numbers posted on site to ask about fees and hours, and check them before you leave.
When you arrange a tour with a tricycle driver, say in advance which of the cave, Patar Beach, falls and lighthouse you want and whether waiting time is included.
The cave floor is wet and slippery and the number of swimmers is limited, so follow the staff's instructions and always accompany children.

Depth varies by spot and with the tide and season. A 2016 local news article put the deepest part at about 8 feet (about 2.4 m), while another guide described it as chest-deep. If you are a weak swimmer, stay in the shallow areas.
It is a private park, so fees, hours and rules can change. Check the latest notice.
There are many stairs, so getting around may be hard for people with limited mobility.
In the rainy season or during typhoons, check road conditions and the weather forecast and adjust your plans.
Some visitors report monkeys playing in the trees, so watch your food bags and valuables.
The town where the cave is located. It is about
15 minutes
from the cave by tricycle and has an old church, restaurants and lodging.
Pangasinan's best-known island attraction. Many travelers combine it with Bolinao on a western Pangasinan trip. Check the transport details separately.
A white sand beach close to the cave. Entry is described as free with a parking fee, and the rock formation area along the shore charges a separate entrance fee in some places.
Located in Barangay Samang Norte. It is about
19km
from town, and the last stretch is a dirt road.
A lighthouse at the tip of the Bolinao peninsula, described as free to visit. Some visitors report that you can see toward it from the cross on the hill at Enchanted Cave park.
